spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m0p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Terminals
VARIABLES version, view, appliedStale, capacity
vars == <<version, view, appliedStale, capacity>>

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ view = [t \in Terminals |-> 0]
  /\ appliedStale = FALSE
  /\ capacity = 2

ReadRecord(t) ==
  /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![t] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, appliedStale, capacity>>

Commit(t) ==
  /\ view[t] = version
  /\ version < capacity
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ appliedStale' = (view[t] # version)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<view, capacity>>

SwitchPresses ==
  /\ capacity' \in 1..3
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, view, appliedStale>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Terminals : ReadRecord(t) \/ Commit(t)
  \/ SwitchPresses

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleCommitApplied == appliedStale = FALSE
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Terminals = {t1, t2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleCommitApplied
nl:
A print shop runs a single shared job-record for the currently active print run, and several operator terminals compete to update it using optimistic locking. Each terminal first reads the record's version number into its own local view, prepares an edit, and later tries to commit. A commit is accepted only if the terminal's cached view still equals the record's live version; otherwise the terminal is stale (someone else committed in between) and it must re-read and retry instead of writing. The shop's print capacity changes at runtime as presses are switched on or off, and the record's version may only advance while it is still below the current capacity ceiling. The system records whether any commit was ever applied by a terminal whose cached view disagreed with the live version at commit time. Terminals that lost the race are expected to loop back through a fresh read.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no commit to the shared job record is ever applied by a terminal whose cached version differs from the record's live version at the moment of commit.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m8p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Routers, Bags
VARIABLES coarse, fine, dispatched
vars == <<coarse, fine, dispatched>>

Init ==
  /\ coarse = "free"
  /\ fine = [b \in Bags |-> "free"]
  /\ dispatched = [b \in Bags |-> 0]

AcquireCoarse(r) ==
  /\ coarse = "free"
  /\ coarse' = r
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, dispatched>>

AcquireFine(r, b) ==
  /\ coarse = r
  /\ fine[b] = "free"
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, dispatched>>

Dispatch(r, b) ==
  /\ coarse = r
  /\ fine[b] = r
  /\ dispatched[b] = 0
  /\ dispatched' = [dispatched EXCEPT ![b] = dispatched[b] + 1]
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = "free"]
  /\ UNCHANGED coarse

ReleaseCoarse(r) ==
  /\ coarse = r
  /\ coarse' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, dispatched>>

Next ==
  \E r \in Routers :
    \/ AcquireCoarse(r) \/ ReleaseCoarse(r)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : AcquireFine(r, b) \/ Dispatch(r, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DispatchedAtMostOnce == \A b \in Bags : dispatched[b] <= 1
====
nl:
An airport baggage router has two independent routing instances that share one pool of chutes and must dispatch each bag onto its chute at most once. To act on a bag, a routing instance must acquire locks hierarchically: first the coarse pool-wide lock, then the fine per-bag lock, and only while holding both may it perform the irreversible dispatch. Because both instances contend for the same coarse lock, only one instance can be manipulating the pool at any time. Once a bag is dispatched, its dispatch count must never rise above one, even though two instances race over the shared pool. After dispatching, an instance releases the coarse lock so the other instance can proceed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every bag is dispatched onto a chute at most once, no matter how the two routing instances interleave.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m1p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Robots
VARIABLES held, transit
vars == <<held, transit>>

Init ==
  /\ held = {CHOOSE r \in Robots : TRUE}
  /\ transit = 0

Release(r) ==
  /\ r \in held
  /\ held' = held \ {r}
  /\ transit' = transit + 1

Deliver(r) ==
  /\ transit > 0
  /\ r \notin held
  /\ transit' = transit - 1
  /\ held' = held \cup {r}

Next == \E r \in Robots : Release(r) \/ Deliver(r)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TokenConserved == Cardinality(held) + transit = 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TokenConserved
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots coordinates exclusive access to a charging bus by circulating a single access token around a logical ring. At any instant the token is either held by exactly one robot or in transit between robots along the ring. A holding robot may release the token, which puts the token into transit, and a transiting token may later be delivered to any robot, because delivery messages can be reordered on the ring. Whether the token is resting with a robot or moving between them, exactly one token exists in the whole system at all times: the ring never manufactures a second token and never loses the one it has. The number of tokens held plus the number in transit is an invariant of the system.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the quantity of access tokens is conserved: robots holding the token plus tokens in transit always sum to exactly one.

spec_text:

  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<view, crashed>>

Crash(t) ==

  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![t] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, view, openPrinted>>

Next == (\E t \in Traders : Observe(t) \/ PrintOpen(t) \/ Crash(t)) \/ UNCHANGED vars

OpenPrintedAtMostOnce == openPrinted <= 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Traders = {g1, g2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OpenPrintedAtMostOnce
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction where several trader gateways race to trigger the single opening print for a symbol. Each gateway observes the auction book's version counter into a local snapshot, then attempts the print using optimistic locking: the print is only allowed if the gateway's snapshot still matches the live version and no opening print has yet occurred. When a gateway prints the opening, the auction version advances so any other gateway's snapshot is now stale and its retry must fail. Any gateway may crash silently at any moment, after which it takes no further action, but its earlier or absent participation must never let a second opening print slip through. The opening print is irreversible: once the market is open it stays open.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the irreversible opening print happens at most once across all trader gateways.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m4p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANT Cap, MaxTickets
VARIABLES queue, applied, admitted
vars == <<queue, applied, admitted>>

Init ==
  /\ queue = << >>
  /\ applied = 0
  /\ admitted = 0

Admit ==
  /\ Len(queue) < Cap
  /\ admitted < MaxTickets
  /\ admitted' = admitted + 1
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, admitted + 1)
  /\ UNCHANGED applied

ApplyAt(i) ==
  /\ i \in 1 .. Len(queue)
  /\ applied' = applied + 1
  /\ queue' = SubSeq(queue, 1, i - 1) \o SubSeq(queue, i + 1, Len(queue))
  /\ UNCHANGED admitted

Next == Admit \/ (\E i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : ApplyAt(i)) \/ UNCHANGED vars
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdates == applied + Len(queue) = admitted
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Cap = 2
CONSTANT MaxTickets = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
nl:
On a car-wash conveyor line, a controller feeds car-treatment update tickets into a bounded staging queue that applies backpressure: no new ticket may be admitted once the queue is full. Each admitted ticket represents one update destined for a shared wash-log record that tallies how many treatments have actually been applied. Worker stations pull tickets from the staging queue in any order, because tickets can be reordered in transit, and each applied ticket increments the shared tally exactly once. The number of tickets ever admitted, the number still waiting in the queue, and the number applied to the log must always stay in balance so no update is silently dropped or double-counted. The queue length is capped and the total number of admitted tickets is bounded.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no update to the shared wash-log is ever lost, meaning the applied tally plus the tickets still queued always equals the number of tickets admitted.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m2p6t0 ----
CONSTANT Stations
VARIABLES vote, decision, crashed
vars == <<vote, decision, crashed>>

Init ==
  /\ vote = [s \in Stations |-> "none"]
  /\ decision = "none"
  /\ crashed = [s \in Stations |-> FALSE]

CastReady(s) ==
  /\ ~crashed[s]
  /\ vote[s] = "none"
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![s] = "ready"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<decision, crashed>>

CastNotReady(s) ==
  /\ ~crashed[s]
  /\ vote[s] = "none"
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![s] = "notready"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<decision, crashed>>

Crash(s) ==
  /\ ~crashed[s]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, decision>>

Commit ==
  /\ decision = "none"
  /\ \A s \in Stations : vote[s] = "ready"
  /\ decision' = "commit"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, crashed>>

Abort ==
  /\ decision = "none"
  /\ \E s \in Stations : (vote[s] = "notready" \/ crashed[s])
  /\ decision' = "abort"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, crashed>>

Next == (\E s \in Stations : CastReady(s) \/ CastNotReady(s) \/ Crash(s)) \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ UNCHANGED vars
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CommitOnlyIfAllReady == (decision = "commit") => (\A s \in Stations : vote[s] = "ready")
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Stations = {s1, s2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CommitOnlyIfAllReady
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line uses two-phase commit to bring a batch of pre-treatment stations into a synchronized wash cycle. A coordinator asks each authorized station in the cohort to vote on whether it is ready; a station may vote ready or not-ready, and any station may crash silently before voting, contributing no vote at all. The coordinator may declare the cycle committed only when every authorized station in the cohort has actually voted ready, so a crashed or non-ready station must block commitment. Otherwise the coordinator declares the cycle aborted. The decision is made once and is never taken by, or on behalf of, a station that did not properly authorize it. No stale or missing participant may cause a commit it never agreed to.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the cycle is committed only if every authorized station voted ready, so no unauthorized or non-voting station can be bound to a commit.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m5p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Surgeries, Slots, Schedulers, Quorum
VARIABLES votes, assignedTo
vars == <<votes, assignedTo>>

Init ==
  /\ votes = [g \in Surgeries |-> {}]
  /\ assignedTo = [g \in Surgeries |-> "none"]

Approve(g, sch) ==
  /\ sch \notin votes[g]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![g] = votes[g] \cup {sch}]
  /\ UNCHANGED assignedTo

Bind(g, s) ==
  /\ assignedTo[g] = "none"
  /\ Cardinality(votes[g]) >= Quorum
  /\ \A h \in Surgeries : assignedTo[h] # s
  /\ assignedTo' = [assignedTo EXCEPT ![g] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED votes

Next ==
  \/ \E g \in Surgeries, sch \in Schedulers : Approve(g, sch)
  \/ \E g \in Surgeries, s \in Slots : Bind(g, s)
  \/ UNCHANGED vars

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A g1, g2 \in Surgeries :
    (g1 # g2 /\ assignedTo[g1] # "none" /\ assignedTo[g2] # "none")
      => assignedTo[g1] # assignedTo[g2]
====
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler decides which surgery is granted each operating-room slot, but no assignment is final until a quorum of on-call schedulers has approved it. Each scheduler independently casts an approval for a proposed surgery, and because approvals travel over an unreliable channel they may arrive in any order. Once a surgery has collected a quorum of approvals and the target slot is not already taken by another surgery, the scheduler binds that surgery to that slot. Two different surgeries must never end up bound to the same operating-room slot, no matter how approvals are interleaved or reordered. Approvals accumulate per surgery and a binding is committed only when the quorum threshold is met.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no operating-room slot is ever double-allocated, that is, two distinct surgeries are never bound to the same slot.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m1p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Machines
VARIABLES grant, dispensed
vars == <<grant, dispensed>>

Init ==
  /\ grant = (CHOOSE m \in Machines : TRUE)
  /\ dispensed = [m \in Machines |-> 0]

PassToRing(m) ==
  /\ grant = m
  /\ grant' = "ring"
  /\ UNCHANGED dispensed

Deliver(m) ==
  /\ grant = "ring"
  /\ grant' = m
  /\ UNCHANGED dispensed

Dispense(m) ==
  /\ grant = m
  /\ dispensed[m] = 0
  /\ dispensed' = [dispensed EXCEPT ![m] = dispensed[m] + 1]
  /\ grant' = "ring"

Next == \E m \in Machines : PassToRing(m) \/ Deliver(m) \/ Dispense(m)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DispensedAtMostOnce == \A m \in Machines : dispensed[m] <= 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Machines = {m1, m2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispensedAtMostOnce
nl:
A network of vending machines shares one restock-dispense authority by circulating a single grant along a logical ring. The grant is either resting at one machine or moving through the ring toward another; because ring messages can be reordered, a moving grant may be delivered to any machine next. Only the machine currently holding the grant may perform the irreversible dispense of its staged product, after which it hands the grant back into the ring. Each machine must dispense at most once: even though the grant keeps circulating, a machine that has already dispensed can never dispense a second time. Dispensing is irreversible because product physically leaves the machine.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every vending machine performs its irreversible dispense at most once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m8p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Banks, Accounts, Capacity
VARIABLES coarse, fine, settled
vars == <<coarse, fine, settled>>

Init ==
  /\ coarse = "free"
  /\ fine = [a \in Accounts |-> "free"]
  /\ settled = 0

AcquireCoarse(bk) ==
  /\ coarse = "free"
  /\ coarse' = bk
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, settled>>

ReleaseCoarse(bk) ==
  /\ coarse = bk
  /\ coarse' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, settled>>

AcquireFine(bk, a) ==
  /\ coarse = bk
  /\ fine[a] = "free"
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![a] = bk]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, settled>>

Post(bk, a) ==
  /\ coarse = bk
  /\ fine[a] = bk
  /\ settled < Capacity
  /\ settled' = settled + 1
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![a] = "free"]
  /\ UNCHANGED coarse

Next ==
  \/ \E bk \in Banks : AcquireCoarse(bk) \/ ReleaseCoarse(bk)
  \/ \E bk \in Banks, a \in Accounts : AcquireFine(bk, a) \/ Post(bk, a)
  \/ UNCHANGED vars

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

WithinCapacity == settled <= Capacity
====
nl:
An interbank settlement batch posts individual transfers under a strict two-level locking discipline. To settle a transfer, a bank must first take the coarse batch-wide lock, and only while holding it may it take the fine per-account lock, and only while holding both may it post one settlement. The batch has a fixed capacity ceiling on the total number of settlements it may post, and settlements may be processed for accounts in any order. Each successful post increments the running count of settled transfers and then frees the fine lock so other accounts can proceed. The running settled count may never exceed the batch's capacity ceiling.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of posted settlements never exceeds the batch capacity ceiling.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m0p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Clients
VARIABLES generation, snapshot, starts
vars == <<generation, snapshot, starts>>

Init ==
  /\ generation = 0
  /\ snapshot = [c \in Clients |-> 0]
  /\ starts = 0

Observe(c) ==
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![c] = generation]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<generation, starts>>

StartMatch(c) ==
  /\ snapshot[c] = generation
  /\ starts = 0
  /\ starts' = 1
  /\ generation' = generation + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED snapshot

Next == (\E c \in Clients : Observe(c) \/ StartMatch(c)) \/ UNCHANGED vars
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StartedAtMostOnce == starts <= 1
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Clients = {p1, p2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT StartedAtMostOnce
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker lets several player clients race to lock in the single match-start for a lobby using optimistic concurrency. Each client observes the lobby's generation counter into a local snapshot, and later tries to start the match only if its snapshot still equals the live generation and the match has not already started. When one client starts the match, the generation advances so every other client's snapshot becomes stale and its start attempt is rejected, forcing a re-observe. Because observation and start attempts can interleave in any order, many clients may hold snapshots at once, yet the match-start is irreversible and must fire at most once for the lobby. A started match cannot be un-started.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the irreversible match-start fires at most once for the lobby.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m5p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Instances, MaxProposals
VARIABLES proposed, applied, acks, inflight
vars == <<proposed, applied, acks, inflight>>

Init ==
  /\ proposed = 0
  /\ applied = 0
  /\ acks = {}
  /\ inflight = FALSE

Propose ==
  /\ ~inflight
  /\ proposed < MaxProposals
  /\ proposed' = proposed + 1
  /\ inflight' = TRUE
  /\ acks' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED applied

Ack(i) ==
  /\ inflight
  /\ i \notin acks
  /\ acks' = acks \cup {i}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, applied, inflight>>

Commit ==
  /\ inflight
  /\ acks = Instances
  /\ applied' = applied + 1
  /\ inflight' = FALSE
  /\ acks' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED proposed

Next == Propose \/ (\E i \in Instances : Ack(i)) \/ Commit \/ UNCHANGED vars
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostRosterUpdate == proposed = applied + (IF inflight THEN 1 ELSE 0)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Instances = {i1, i2}
CONSTANT MaxProposals = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostRosterUpdate
nl:
Two independent scheduler instances share one operating-room roster and coordinate every roster update through quorum acknowledgement so no update is ever lost. At most one update proposal is in flight at a time: one instance proposes the next roster change, then each instance must acknowledge it, and only when both instances (the full quorum) have acknowledged is the update committed into the shared roster. The number of proposals ever raised, the applied updates recorded in the roster, and whether one proposal is currently in flight must always stay in balance, so no acknowledged update is dropped and no committed update is counted twice. Proposals are bounded in number.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no roster update is lost, meaning the number of proposals raised always equals the applied updates plus one if a proposal is currently in flight.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m4p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANTS Cells, Drones, Cap
VARIABLES queue, owners, crashed
vars == <<queue, owners, crashed>>

Init ==
  /\ queue = << >>
  /\ owners = [c \in Cells |-> 0]
  /\ crashed = [d \in Drones |-> FALSE]

Enqueue(c) ==
  /\ Len(queue) < Cap
  /\ owners[c] = 0
  /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : queue[i] # c
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, c)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owners, crashed>>

Take(d) ==
  /\ ~crashed[d]
  /\ queue # << >>
  /\ owners[Head(queue)] = 0
  /\ owners' = [owners EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = owners[Head(queue)] + 1]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Crash(d) ==
  /\ ~crashed[d]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, owners>>

Next == (\E c \in Cells : Enqueue(c)) \/ (\E d \in Drones : Take(d) \/ Crash(d)) \/ UNCHANGED vars
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleSurvey == \A c \in Cells : owners[c] <= 1
====
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm pulls survey assignments from a bounded dispatch queue that applies backpressure: no new grid cell may be queued once the queue is full. Each queued cell must be surveyed by at most one drone, so when a drone takes the next cell off the queue it becomes the sole owner of that cell's assignment. A drone may crash silently at any time and then takes no further assignments, but a crash must never cause a cell to be handed to a second drone. The count of drones assigned to any given cell must never rise above one. Cells are pulled from the queue in order and the queue length is capped.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no grid cell is ever double-allocated, that is, at most one drone is assigned to survey any given cell.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m2p6t3 ----
CONSTANT Players
VARIABLES yesVotes, noVotes, decision
vars == <<yesVotes, noVotes, decision>>

Init ==
  /\ yesVotes = {}
  /\ noVotes = {}
  /\ decision = "pending"

VoteYes(p) ==
  /\ p \notin yesVotes
  /\ p \notin noVotes
  /\ yesVotes' = yesVotes \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<noVotes, decision>>

VoteNo(p) ==
  /\ p \notin yesVotes
  /\ p \notin noVotes
  /\ noVotes' = noVotes \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVotes, decision>>

Commit ==
  /\ decision = "pending"
  /\ yesVotes = Players
  /\ decision' = "started"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVotes, noVotes>>

Abort ==
  /\ decision = "pending"
  /\ noVotes # {}
  /\ decision' = "aborted"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yesVotes, noVotes>>

Next == (\E p \in Players : VoteYes(p) \/ VoteNo(p)) \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ UNCHANGED vars
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CommitOnlyIfAllYes == (decision = "started") => (yesVotes = Players)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Players = {p1, p2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CommitOnlyIfAllYes
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker starts a ranked match only through a two-phase commit across the invited players. Each authorized player casts either a yes or a no vote, and a player may be slow, leaving its vote outstanding for a long time, but it never crashes and its vote must still be counted before any commit. The coordinator may declare the match started (committed) only when every authorized player has voted yes; if any player votes no, the match is aborted. A slow, not-yet-voted player must therefore block the commit rather than be silently assumed to agree. No player who did not vote yes may be bound to a started match.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the match is committed only when every authorized player has voted yes, so no un-consenting or slow player is bound to a start.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m6p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, MaxClock
VARIABLES holders, expiry, clock
vars == <<holders, expiry, clock>>

Init ==
  /\ holders = [b \in Blocks |-> {}]
  /\ expiry = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ clock = 0

Acquire(t, b) ==
  /\ holders[b] = {}
  /\ holders' = [holders EXCEPT ![b] = {t}]
  /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![b] = clock + 2]
  /\ UNCHANGED clock

Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxClock
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ holders' = [b \in Blocks |-> IF expiry[b] <= clock + 1 THEN {} ELSE holders[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED expiry

AdminRelease(b) ==
  /\ holders' = [holders EXCEPT ![b] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, clock>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Acquire(t, b)
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : AdminRelease(b)
  \/ UNCHANGED vars

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoConflictingLease == \A b \in Blocks : Cardinality(holders[b]) <= 1
====
nl:
A subway signalling system grants trains exclusive ownership of track blocks using time-bounded leases. A train acquires a block only when the block currently has no valid holder, and the lease is stamped with an expiry a fixed interval ahead of the current clock. As the clock advances, any lease whose expiry has passed is cleared, freeing the block for others. A privileged control-room admin may override and force-release any block regardless of its lease. Because a block must carry a train safely, it must never be held under a valid lease by two trains at once, no matter how acquisitions, expiries, and admin overrides interleave.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no track block is ever simultaneously held under a valid lease by more than one train.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m8p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Trains, Ceiling
VARIABLES coarse, inner, occupancy
vars == <<coarse, inner, occupancy>>

Init ==
  /\ coarse = "free"
  /\ inner = "free"
  /\ occupancy = 0

AcquireCoarse(t) == coarse = "free" /\ coarse' = t /\ UNCHANGED <<inner, occupancy>>
AcquireInner(t) == coarse = t /\ inner = "free" /\ inner' = t /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, occupancy>>

Enter(t) ==
  /\ inner = t
  /\ occupancy < Ceiling
  /\ occupancy' = occupancy + 1
  /\ inner' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED coarse

Leave ==
  /\ occupancy > 0
  /\ occupancy' = occupancy - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, inner>>

AdminOverride ==
  /\ coarse' = "free"
  /\ inner' = "free"
  /\ UNCHANGED occupancy

Next ==

---- MODULE W4Od1m3p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxEpoch

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ leader = (CHOOSE c \in Controllers : TRUE)
  /\ cached = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
  /\ staleActed = FALSE

Failover(c) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ leader' = c
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![c] = epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED staleActed

Sync(c) ==
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, leader, staleActed>>

Assign(c) ==
  /\ leader = c
  /\ cached[c] = epoch
  /\ staleActed' = (cached[c] # epoch)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, leader, cached>>

AdminOverride(c) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ leader' = c
  /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![c] = epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED staleActed

Next == (\E c \in Controllers : Failover(c) \/ Sync(c) \/ Assign(c) \/ AdminOverride(c)) \/ UNCHANGED vars

The system flags whether any assignment was ever performed by a controller whose cached epoch did not match the true epoch at that moment.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m2p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Cars, Instances
VARIABLES occupants, candidate, votes
vars == <<occupants, candidate, votes>>

Init ==
  /\ occupants = {}
  /\ candidate = "none"
  /\ votes = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]

Propose(car) ==
  /\ candidate = "none"
  /\ occupants = {}
  /\ candidate' = car
  /\ votes' = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED occupants

CastVote(i) ==
  /\ candidate # "none"
  /\ ~votes[i]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupants, candidate>>

Enter ==
  /\ candidate # "none"
  /\ \A i \in Instances : votes[i]
  /\ occupants = {}
  /\ occupants' = {candidate}
  /\ candidate' = "none"
  /\ votes' = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]

Exit(car) ==
  /\ car \in occupants
  /\ occupants' = occupants \ {car}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<candidate, votes>>

Next ==
  \/ \E car \in Cars : Propose(car) \/ Exit(car)
  \/ \E i \in Instances : CastVote(i)
  \/ Enter
  \/ UNCHANGED vars

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BayMutualExclusion == Cardinality(occupants) <= 1
====
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line admits cars into a single critical wash bay, and two controller instances share the one bay pool. Admission uses two-phase commit: a candidate car is proposed, then both controller instances must vote to admit it, and only when both have voted and the bay is empty does the car enter the bay. A car in the bay must exit before any other car can be admitted, so the bay holds at most one car at any time despite the two instances coordinating. The mutual-exclusion guarantee on the wash bay must hold across all interleavings of proposals, votes, entries, and exits.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the critical wash bay holds at most one car at any time (mutual exclusion).
